title: Turkish Shipyard Mengi Yay Launches First 52.5m Explorer Yacht Gray Wolf
description: Mengi Yay launches Gray Wolf, the first hull in its flagship Virtus XP series, marking the largest yacht built by the Turkish shipyard to date.
html:
Turkish Shipyard Delivers First 52.5-Metre Explorer Yacht With Advanced Naval Architecture

The Turkish shipyard Mengi Yay has successfully launched Gray Wolf, the inaugural vessel in its flagship 52.5-metre Virtus XP series, from its facilities in Tuzla. Previously designated as NB113, this steel and aluminium motor yacht now stands as the largest yacht ever constructed by the shipyard, representing a significant milestone in the builder’s evolution and market positioning within the global superyacht industry. Gray Wolf embodies the collaborative vision of several renowned maritime professionals. The exterior and interior design comes from long-standing partners VYD Studio, while Van Oossanen Naval Architects engineered the hull and systems. Antalyacht provided owner’s representation throughout the construction phase, ensuring meticulous attention to the client’s specifications and requirements.

The vessel’s technical specifications underscore its capability as a true “go anywhere” explorer. With an 8.9-metre beam, a 2.6-metre draught at full load, and a volume just under 500 gross tonnes, Gray Wolf achieves an optimal balance between seaworthiness and operational efficiency. The yacht is RINA C+ classed and complies with REG Yacht Code, DMS, and Ice Class Comfort Class standards, positioning it for extended global cruising in challenging environments. Accommodation spans five cabins arranged across multiple decks, with the master suite occupying a prominent position on the main deck in an open-plan configuration. Interior renderings reveal a contemporary aesthetic dominated by a refined white palette and expansive floor-to-ceiling glazing that floods the spaces with natural light. The main saloon features curved seating arrangements centred around a coffee table, while an adjacent formal dining area provides elegant entertaining space.

Outdoor living takes centre stage across multiple deck areas. A swimming pool on the main deck, combined with a Jacuzzi positioned at the bow, creates dedicated wellness zones. The upper deck features a helipad that transforms into a lounge when not in operational use—a practical design solution increasingly favoured by explorer yacht owners. The sundeck incorporates a forward-facing bar with panoramic ocean views, complemented by sunlounger arrangements and an outdoor dining configuration that facilitates al fresco entertaining. Performance characteristics align with the yacht’s explorer pedigree. Gray Wolf is expected to achieve a maximum speed of 15 knots, cruise comfortably at 12 knots, and maintain a range of approximately 6,000 nautical miles at 10-knot transit speed. These figures reflect the engineering philosophy of prioritising efficiency and endurance over raw velocity—a hallmark of serious expedition vessels.

Following her launch, Gray Wolf is scheduled to commence sea trials in the coming weeks, with delivery anticipated for summer 2026. The yacht will make its international debut at the Monaco Yacht Show in September 2026, where it will be presented to the global superyacht market and prospective clientele seeking capable explorer vessels with refined accommodations. Mengi Yay’s current order book demonstrates robust market demand for its product line. The shipyard has six yachts actively under construction, including the first unit in its NL50 Plus series, designed by the acclaimed Nuvolari Lenard studio. This pipeline underscores the builder’s strengthened position within the competitive Turkish shipbuilding sector and its appeal to owners seeking quality construction combined with innovative design.

The launch of Gray Wolf represents more than a single delivery; it signals Mengi Yay’s successful transition into the larger explorer yacht segment and validates its design partnerships with internationally respected studios. As the superyacht market continues to favour capable, long-range vessels over pure size and speed, Gray Wolf’s arrival offers a compelling proposition for discerning owners planning extended global voyages with the comfort and technology expected of contemporary superyachts.
